query: Prepare a one-page briefing for a meeting with Databricks on 17 November 2026. Cover what changed in the last 30 days (news, launches, hires, deals), cite a source URL for every fact, and end with three open questions to ask.
briefing:
# Databricks Briefing: 16 October to 15 November 2026

*Prepared for the meeting on 17 November 2026. Items are ordered by materiality within each category.*

## 1. News

- **Second-generation Genie launched on 11 November 2026.** Databricks describes Genie as an always-on, autonomous enterprise agent that takes goals, delegates to sub-agents, and contacts users only when a decision is needed. It is governed by Unity Catalog permissions and Unity Gateway budgets and approval rules. Pricing is usage-based rather than per seat, and Databricks says more than 20,000 organizations use the platform, including 70% of the Fortune 500. [Source URL not captured in research; confirm on the Databricks newsroom before the meeting.]
- **Europe and Middle East investment of about $3 billion, announced 11 November 2026.** Databricks says this is its largest regional investment outside North America, over three years. It will fund Lakebase, Genie and Unity Gateway work, expand the EMEA team by about 50% (from more than 2,000 employees), open four offices (Amsterdam, Milan, Zurich, Frankfurt), and train about 500,000 people in data and AI skills by 2030 [1]. **Date discrepancy:** HPCwire dates the announcement 12 November [8]. Superpower Daily corroborates the investment without a day [9].

## 2. Product Launches

- **Genie expansion (11 November).** Genie Ontology is generally available. Genie Search, Ontology Manager and the always-on Genie are described as "coming soon" to preview and beta [1][2]. The November release notes, however, list Genie Search and Genie Ontology as GA [2]. **This conflict is unresolved** and should be clarified with Databricks.
- **Apache Spark 4.3.0 (30 October 2026)** is the open-source release that introduces stateful real-time streaming. Databricks made it available in Databricks Runtime 19 [6][7]. Databricks says Spark moves to a quarterly feature-release cadence [7].
- **October generally available releases:**
  - Transactions for managed Delta and Iceberg tables (14 October) [3].
  - Real-time mode in Lakeflow pipelines on classic and serverless compute (29 October) [5].
  - Genie Code tasks in Lakeflow Jobs (21 October) [3].
  - Agentic code converter for SQL targets (15 October) [3].
  - Feature Views for batch, streaming and request-time data (12 October) [3].
- **October previews and betas:** a Jailbreak guardrail for MCP tool calls in Unity Gateway (21 October, Beta) and DataFrame caching on serverless compute (23 October, Public Preview) [3].
- **November items:**
  - Genie ZeroOps in Beta, which monitors jobs and pipelines and proposes fixes (12 November) [2].
  - OAuth on-behalf-of for service principals generally available (12 November) [2].
  - Managed warehouse for MLflow in Beta (2 November) [4].
  - Gemini 3.6 Flash retires on 19 November, with calls redirected to Gemini 3.8 Flash [2].

## 3. Executive and Notable Hires

- No executive hire, departure or appointment dated within the window was found in the research.
- Samuel Bonamigo is quoted as SVP and General Manager, EMEA, in the 11 November release. The release does not describe his appointment, so no hire can be confirmed [1].

## 4. Deals

- **Investment and partnerships:** The $3 billion EMEA plan [1] is the main deal item. The same release references startup investments made in the past six months: Tsuga, Advancing Analytics (through Databricks Ventures) and Applied Computing (through the AI Accelerator Program). It also names customers ABN Amro, adidas, Danone, Heineken, HelloFresh, Mercedes-Benz and Nationwide [1]. None of these is dated within the window, and the release gives no allocation of the $3 billion.
- **Flagged, not verified (no verifiable URL captured, so excluded from the main findings):**
  - Reuters joining the Databricks marketplace (about 6 November). Only an X post was seen.
  - Databricks Ventures' Reflex Series A ($15M, 29 October). The only source is an aggregator profile.
  - More than $500M Netherlands investment (10 November). It is referenced but was not opened.
  - Fox Corporation selecting Databricks as strategic partner (13 October).

## Three Open Questions for the Meeting

1. Which Genie components are generally available today: Genie Search and Genie Ontology, which the release notes list as GA, or the "coming soon" status in the launch announcement? What is the timeline for the always-on Genie?
2. How will the $3 billion EMEA investment be allocated across Lakebase, Genie, Unity Gateway, engineering hubs and customer teams, and does the Netherlands investment form part of that envelope?
3. Genie is now priced by usage rather than per seat, with spend limits set in Unity Gateway. How do customers forecast costs for always-on agents, and how is pricing expected to change as Genie Search and the always-on Genie move from preview to general availability?

---

### Sources

[1] Databricks to Invest ~$3 Billion Across Europe and the Middle East (Databricks newsroom): https://www.databricks.com/company/newsroom/press-releases/databricks-invest-3-billion-across-europe-and-middle-east
[2] Databricks platform release notes index (AWS docs): https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product
[3] Databricks AWS release notes, October 2026: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october
[4] Databricks AWS release notes, November 2026: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november
[5] Azure Databricks release notes, October 2026 (Microsoft Learn): https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/release-notes/product/2026/october
[6] Apache Spark 4.3.0 released: https://spark.apache.org/news/spark-4-3-0-released.html
[7] Introducing Apache Spark 4.3, now available in Databricks Runtime 19 (Databricks blog): https://www.databricks.com/blog/introducing-apache-spark-43-now-available-databricks-runtime-19
[8] Databricks plans $3B investment in Europe and the Middle East (BigDATAwire/HPCwire): https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/this-just-in/databricks-plans-3b-investment-in-europe-and-the-middle-east
[9] Databricks outlines $3 billion investment in Europe and the Middle East (Superpower Daily): https://superpowerdaily.com/posts/databricks-outlines-3-billion-investment-in-europe-and-the-middle-east
